notes: Adds FindAllImportStatements with config-level parent override and keeps the now-unused FindImportStatements map wrapper that encodes the buggy first-block-only semantics; the cross-module per-instance case is still lost.

Fixes the root-module case, but it keeps the old buggy map-returning FindImportStatements as dead API, and its config-resource-level parent override still silently drops child-module imports that target different instances.

Fixes same-module multi-instance imports by returning a slice, but a parent import still overrides a child at the config-resource level, so child imports for other instances are still silently dropped (unlike the reference's per-instance dedup); adds a useful unit test and an integration test.

Correctly switches to a slice so same-module blocks survive, but the cross-module override is still per ConfigResource rather than per instance, so a parent and child importing different instances loses the child's block; it adds a good unit test and an integration test.

Essentially the same as C1: a slice with config-resource-level parent override, which fixes the reported root case but still discards child-module imports for other instances; only a single root-level regression test.

Minimal slice-based change that fixes same-module for_each imports, but it still discards child-module imports of other instances whenever a parent touches the same resource; there is only a single root-case test.

Same config-level override as C3 and also keeps the legacy dropping API (even tests it); its for_each/count and root/child/root-into-child tests are thorough but encode semantics that still drop child imports for different instances.

Functionally the same as C1, with thorough table-driven tests over for_each/count and root/child placements, but it leaves a misleading dead first-per-resource API and keeps config-level cross-module dedup that drops distinct child instances.

Statically parses each `to` address so a parent only overrides a child when they target the same instance, handling the cross-module different-instance case; it still conservatively drops child imports when either address is dynamic and ignores module instance keys, and has only one root-level test.

Closest to correct: it compares statically parsed instance addresses against all prior statements, so parent/child imports of different instances both survive, but dynamic (for_each) imports and expanded-module keys are handled imprecisely instead of deduping after expansion like the reference; there is only a root test.

Instance-aware override like C5, but the claimed map is overwritten by each new statement, so the override check only compares against the latest claim and is order-dependent (a parent's import of an instance can fail to override the child's); it also adds hidden fields to the struct and has a misleading comment, though it includes root and child-module tests.

Statically parsing `to` lets parent and child import different instances, but the `claimed` map keeps only the last statement, so a parent with several imports may fail to override a matching child instance; it also adds private fields to an exported struct, and dynamic targets are conservatively dropped.
